analysis.explanation: The Random Forest classified this binary as malware with probability 0.985, and all 20 top n-grams have positive SHAP values (+0.0051 to +0.0102), so every listed feature pushes toward cryptojacking and none offset it. The strongest signals are consistent with hashing or cipher routines. ADD ROR (rank 1, +0.01018, freq 0.001022), ROL ADD (rank 6, +0.006726), and MOV ROL (rank 19, +0.005192) are rotate-and-add sequences typical of ARX-style mixing. BSWAP LEA (rank 11, +0.005972) fits byte-order conversion of hash state. Several SIMD n-grams are also frequent: MOVDQA MOVAPS (+0.007883), PXOR MOVAPS (+0.007858), PXOR MOVUPS (+0.006683), PXOR PXOR (+0.005945), and PXOR MOVDQA (+0.005225). Each has a frequency of about 0.0005 to 0.0013, which suggests vectorized XOR and data movement, as seen in memory-hard hashing or bulk state manipulation. The x87 and scalar floating-point n-grams (ADD FLD, FSTP MOV, MOV FLD, MOVAPD DIVSD) are rare, but they have notable SHAP weight and may indicate numeric or auxiliary computation. The remaining n-grams (POP SUB, CALL RET, ADD PUSH, CALL MOVQ, SUB CMOVG, POP LEA, MOVZX PUSH) are generic control-flow, stack, and data-handling patterns. They contribute to the model's decision but are not specific by themselves. The evidence contains no function-level or API detail, so conclusions rest only on the n-gram statistics. The combination of rotate/add mixing, byte swapping, and dense SIMD XOR activity, together with the high model probability and uniformly positive SHAP, supports a high-confidence cryptojacking assessment. The absence of function names and the generic nature of some n-grams keep confidence below certainty.

Generic arithmetic-then-stack sequence. It has weak standalone meaning but contributes positively to the model.
Rare x87 floating-point load after addition. It suggests numeric or legacy FP code, which may come from a bundled library.

key_indicators: All 20 top n-grams have positive SHAP toward cryptojacking
Rotate/add ARX patterns (ADD ROR, ROL ADD, MOV ROL) typical of hashing
BSWAP LEA byte-order handling consistent with hash state processing
Dense SIMD XOR/move patterns (PXOR, MOVDQA, MOVAPS, MOVUPS) at about 0.05–0.13% frequency
Floating-point n-grams (FLD, FSTP, DIVSD) with notable SHAP weight
analysis.recommended_action: Treat as likely cryptojacking malware. Isolate the sample and analyze it in a sandbox. Locate the functions that contain the rotate/add and SIMD XOR sequences and check whether they implement a mining hash algorithm. Inspect network behavior for connections to mining pools and check for persistence and high sustained CPU usage. Use the findings to build detection signatures and IOCs.
